key_insight: Training language models on structured experimental evidence enabled stronger perovskite reasoning and guided a solar-cell contact choice that outperformed the expert-preferred alternative.
engineering_relevance: Evidence-grounded AI could help engineers select interface materials and prioritize experiments for more efficient, thermally stable perovskite solar cells.
method: Reconstruct expert-calibrated evidence records from 4,035 articles, linking strategies, controls, observations and mechanisms.
Adapt OpenPerov using structured evidence; refine selected responses with retrieved evidence in OpenPerov Pro.
Experimentally test an AI-selected K analogue against an expert-preferred Na analogue for self-assembled monolayer design.
evidence_signal: On the 800-question PSM-Bench, OpenPerov Flash ranked first among 13 closed-book systems; experimentally, the selected contact enabled 27.05% efficiency and 96.74% efficiency retention after 1,000 h of dark thermal ageing at 85 °C.
watch_item: Validation in one contact-design comparison and under dark thermal ageing does not establish broad design reliability or long-term stability under operating conditions.
paper_title: Evidence-grounded large language models guide perovskite solar cell design and optimization
